races.title: State Assembly, District 51
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Rick Chavez Zbur
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented Assembly District 51 since December 2022. Attorney at Latham & Watkins for over 25 years, partner from 1994. Executive Director of Equality California from 2014. Former board president of California Environmental Voters. Ran for Congress in 1996.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California; California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO; California Nurses Association; National Union of Healthcare Workers; California Environmental Voters; Equality California; West Hollywood Beverly Hills Democratic Club (2026 election)

cands.gaps: We could not find which bills he sponsored or authored; the Ballotpedia list was empty on the page we read, and his campaign site descriptions are his own claims. We found no statements or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, H-1B visas, school choice or teacher pay. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys.

local.label: Roots 55: He was born and raised in New Mexico and moved to Los Angeles in 1985 as an adult, about 40 years ago, and still lives there.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since December 2022. Before that, Latham & Watkins environmental and government law attorney for over 25 years (partner 1994), then Executive Director of Equality California from 2014.
qual.why: Prior legislative service plus a long law and policy career fits the rubric's high band. Board service is not counted.
qual.label: Prior legislative service plus a long law and policy career fits the rubric's high band. Board service is not counted.

pro-life.evidence: Says he is strongly pro-choice and will always defend legal abortion and access to contraception. He also says he worked to fund Planned Parenthood and to shield abortion patients and providers from out-of-state legal attacks.

workers-first.evidence: Says he is fighting to block Trump and ICE from attacking immigrant communities, and describes having fought ICE overreach in the Legislature.

second-amendment.evidence: Says he has worked to keep guns away from dangerous people by strengthening protections when someone makes violent or hate-based threats. His bio cites commonsense gun safety reform.

back-police-order.evidence: Says he helped pass a bipartisan law giving police and prosecutors stronger tools against organized retail theft and repeat offenders, while also favoring prevention and treatment.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: He was born and raised in New Mexico and moved to Los Angeles in 1985 as an adult, about 40 years ago, and still lives there.

cands.name: Colin D. Hernandez
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for California State Assembly District 51. Political science graduate of the University of Colorado Boulder (2014). Says he has worked at Equality California, Americans for Tax Fairness and the Vera Institute of Justice on LGBTQ+ rights, tax policy, criminal justice and immigration reform, and homelessness. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Candidate-listed endorsers (Ballotpedia survey): LA City Controller Kenneth Mejia, CAIR Action, PALAD, Burbank Councilmember Konstantine Anthony, JVP-LA founder Estee Chandler, Oliver Ma, Maebe Pudlo and UCLA YDSA.
Ballotpedia also lists voter-guide recommendations from Sway groups, including 'Jess's Progressive Picks', 'Mamdanification' and 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress'.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Hernandez holding public office, so there are no official actions to report. His specific job titles and dates at Equality California, Americans for Tax Fairness and the Vera Institute of Justice were not found. We found nothing on his positions on data centers, abortion, gun laws, police pay, or teacher pay. His campaign issues page was cut off before the end, so his full stance on taxes and immigration may not be captured. His birthplace and upbringing come only from his own statements; no independent source was found.

local.label: Roots 100: He says he is a 9th-generation Californian, born and raised in Los Angeles, who has lived in California nearly all his life; this is self-reported on his campaign site and Ballotpedia survey.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He reports advocacy and policy work at Equality California, Americans for Tax Fairness and the Vera Institute of Justice. He has held no elected office.
qual.why: Policy and advocacy work at nonprofits fits the middle range for a legislative job. There is no legislative or local elected service. His job titles and dates were not available, so the score is moderate.
qual.label: Policy and advocacy work at nonprofits fits the middle range for a legislative job. There is no legislative or local elected service. His job titles and dates were not available, so the score is moderate.

land-for-floridians.evidence: He says he will fight to restrict private equity and corporate investment firms in the housing market and to institute vacancy taxes per empty unit.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: He says California must build housing much faster and more easily, cut red tape, reexamine single-family zoning to allow more multifamily housing, and take on wealthy NIMBYs. He says he will always vote to increase housing density.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: He says he will fight to reform Prop 13 and close loopholes that let corporations pay low property taxes, citing school funding. This is a commercial-property focus, and no statement on homeowner taxes was found.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site lists 'Abolish ICE, Protect Immigrants' as a core issue. He says he supports protecting immigrants from unlawful deportations.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: He says 'Public dollars should go to public schools' and that Prop 98 money must stay with public schools. He did not address vouchers, charters or teacher pay in the text read.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 5 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: He says he is a 9th-generation Californian, born and raised in Los Angeles, who has lived in California nearly all his life; this is self-reported on his campaign site and Ballotpedia survey.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Calls for allowing more types of housing, making building 'way easier and faster', re-examining single-family zoning, and increasing density and transit. Says 'Urbanization in our towns and cities will save this state.'
